articles.title: Half of America No Longer Trusts the CDC. For South Asians Who Grew Up Trusting Public Health, the Ground Just Shifted.
articles.excerpt: A Harvard poll finds trust in the CDC has cratered from 77 to 50 per cent in a single year. For a diaspora that built its American life around institutional credibility, the fallout is personal.
articles.image_caption: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention headquarters campus in Atlanta, Georgia

sources.label: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health / de Beaumont Foundation Public Health Listening Lab Poll 2026
Scientific American
American Psychiatric Association May 2026 Mental Health Survey

articles.nri_angle: South Asians in America rely heavily on CDC guidance for childhood vaccinations, travel health, and disease alerts. Many first-generation immigrants came from a system where AIIMS and ICMR guidance carries institutional weight. The collapse of CDC trust creates a unique dilemma for NRI families who split time between India and the US, where immunisation schedules differ and the CDC was the tiebreaker.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Raised Cancer Survivors' Death Risk by 60 Per Cent. The Tobacco Playbook That Built the Industry Is Now Public.
articles.excerpt: A 15-year study shows UPFs sharply increase cancer mortality. A separate paper reveals US tobacco companies used cigarette-marketing tactics to push the same products worldwide.
articles.image_caption: Ultra-processed foods in consumer packaging — a new study links their consumption to a 60 per cent increase in cancer survivors' mortality risk (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention
American Journal of Public Health — Fazzino et al. 2026
Frontiers in Nutrition — UPF and mortality cohort study 2026
Knowridge Science Report

articles.nri_angle: The traditional Indian kitchen is one of the lowest-UPF diets in the world, but second- and third-generation Indian Americans have shifted heavily toward packaged foods. The Indian grocery aisle — frozen parathas, instant upma, ready-to-eat dal — uses the same industrial processes as Western UPFs. For NRI families, the gap between home-cooked and packaged desi food is a health fault line hiding in plain sight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Organs Age at Different Speeds. A New Study Found the Sleep Range That Slows All of Them Down.
articles.excerpt: Columbia researchers built organ-specific aging clocks from brain, heart, lung and immune data. The sweet spot was not eight hours.
articles.image_caption: Columbia University Irving Medical Center in Washington Heights, where researchers identified the sleep range that slows organ aging (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Nature (2026) — Junhao Wen et al., Columbia University
Radiology Site
Fox News Health — Dr. Saema Tahir commentary

articles.title: A Common Diabetes Drug Just Prevented Heart Failure in People Carrying a Genetic Time Bomb.
articles.excerpt: Harvard and MIT researchers found that dapagliflozin cut heart failure hospitalisations by 82 per cent in carriers of cardiomyopathy gene variants. Most had no idea they were at risk.
articles.image_caption: Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, part of the research team that found metformin prevents heart failure in genetically at-risk patients (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Nature Medicine (2026) — Marston, Kany et al.
Fox News Health

articles.title: Your Gut Has Its Own Clock. A New Study Shows Eating After Midnight Breaks It.
articles.excerpt: Researchers at UT Southwestern found that one type of intestinal cell refuses to adjust when you eat at the wrong time, creating a mismatch that lasts for weeks. For South Asians who eat late and work shifts, the implications are personal.
articles.image_caption: A visualisation of the circadian rhythm — the internal clock that new research shows extends to the gut, with eating after midnight disrupting its function (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Million Prescriptions in Five Months. The Obesity Pill Is Here.
articles.excerpt: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill is now one of the fastest pharmaceutical launches in US history. With 80 per cent of users new to GLP-1 therapy, the oral obesity revolution is pulling in people who would never have taken a weekly injection — including the South Asians who need it most.
articles.image_caption: Semaglutide, the active compound behind the oral obesity pill that has reached 3 million prescriptions in five months (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Government's Own Alcohol Study Was Buried. Now It's Out, and the Numbers Are Brutal.
articles.excerpt: A federally commissioned study finds no safe level of drinking. Two drinks a day gives American men a 1-in-25 chance of dying from alcohol. The Trump administration chose not to use it.
articles.image_caption: Alcoholic beverages — a long-suppressed US government study reveals significantly greater health harm than previously acknowledged
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three Americans Now Skip the Doctor Because They Cannot Afford It. The System May Be Three Years From Collapse.
articles.excerpt: New data shows 36 per cent of Americans delayed care in the past six months. Healthcare leaders say the system hits an existential tipping point by 2029. For NRIs navigating insurance on a visa, the math is even worse.
articles.image_caption: An American hospital — one in three adults now reports delaying or skipping medical care because of cost
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Brain Starts Changing After Just Two Minutes of Meditation. A Harvard Study Says the Peak Comes at Seven.
articles.excerpt: An Indian-origin neuroscientist used EEG scans on 103 adults and found that breath-watching shifts brain waves from scattered to focused in under 120 seconds. The technique has roots older than Western medicine itself.
articles.image_caption: New Harvard research finds measurable brain changes begin after just two minutes of meditation
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Most Powerful Obesity Drug Ever Tested Just Crushed Sleep Apnea and Knee Pain in a Single Trial. South Asians Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide, which targets three hormones at once, reduced sleep apnea severity by 61 per cent and knee pain by 73 per cent while delivering 28 per cent body weight loss. For a community with the highest rates of metabolic disease in the world, this is not just another headline.
articles.image_caption: Eli Lilly headquarters in Indianapolis, Indiana — home of the company behind retatrutide
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: It Is Not How Much You Walk. It Is How You Walk. A New Study Says the Difference Is 67 Per Cent.
articles.excerpt: A UK Biobank study of over 6,000 adults found that consolidating the same number of steps into continuous 10-to-15-minute walks — instead of scattering them across the day — reduced cardiovascular events by up to 67 per cent. For South Asians, who carry the world's highest heart disease burden, this reframes everything.
articles.image_caption: Morning walkers in a park — new research shows continuous walking sessions protect the heart far more than scattered steps throughout the day
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Doctors Are Finally Getting Nutrition Training. It Still Will Not Cover Your Dadi's Kitchen.
articles.excerpt: Seventy-three US medical schools have pledged 40 hours of nutrition education. For South Asian patients, that is still not the right 40 hours.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Indian thali — US medical nutrition training still doesn't account for South Asian dietary traditions (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Vaccine That Prevents Cancer Before It Starts Just Got the Green Light. Here Is Why South Asians Should Care.
articles.excerpt: Oxford and Moderna's INTERCEPT-Lynch trial is the first mRNA vaccine designed to stop hereditary cancers from ever forming. The first patient will be dosed this summer.
articles.image_caption: A vaccine being administered — mRNA technology is now being tested to prevent cancer before it starts (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A South Asian Man Reversed His Diabetes for a Decade. He Did It Without Giving Up Indian Food.
articles.excerpt: A Frontiers in Nutrition case study documents ten years of medication-free type 2 diabetes remission using a culturally adapted low-carbohydrate vegetarian diet — and it may hold the key to the diaspora's biggest health crisis.
articles.image_caption: A blood glucose monitoring test — the daily reality for millions of South Asians living with type 2 diabetes
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Antibiotic Resistance Genes Now Contaminate Every Ocean on Earth. India's Coastline Is One of the Most Exposed.
articles.excerpt: A three-year Italian-led study found drug-resistant DNA, microplastics, and forever chemicals across all major ocean basins — with the highest concentrations near populated coasts and shipping routes.
articles.image_caption: Antimicrobial resistance has spread to every major ocean basin, including waters far from coastlines (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Scientists Found the Molecular Switch That Drives Alzheimer's Brain Inflammation. It Can Be Turned Off.
articles.excerpt: A Scripps Research team identified a single chemical modification on the STING protein that locks the brain's immune system into overdrive. Blocking it preserved memory-critical synapses in mice.
articles.image_caption: A PET scan comparing a healthy brain (left) with one affected by Alzheimer's disease — researchers have now identified the molecular switch driving the inflammation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Gut Bacterium Can Decide Whether You Survive Sepsis. Your Diet May Have Already Chosen Sides.
articles.excerpt: A Nature study found that one bacterial strain in the gut dropped survival rates from near-certain to 10 per cent. The implications for South Asian hospital patients and diaspora diets are profound.
articles.image_caption: Rod-shaped bacteria viewed under high magnification microscopy
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Crease in Your Earlobe May Be Warning You About Your Heart. South Asians Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: A diagonal line across the earlobe — known as Frank's sign — has been linked to coronary artery disease for over 50 years. A 2026 diagnostic model says it may be one of the strongest independent predictors of cardiac risk, and the community most vulnerable to heart disease is the least likely to know about it.
articles.image_caption: Coronary artery disease — a condition that research increasingly links to visible markers such as the diagonal earlobe crease known as Frank's sign

articles.title: Global Mental Health Just Hit Its Lowest Recorded Level. The Diaspora's Silence Makes It Worse.
articles.excerpt: The 2026 AXA Mind Health Report surveyed 19,000 adults across 18 countries and found 46 per cent are languishing or struggling. Among younger generations, that number is 59 per cent. South Asian Americans remain among the least likely to seek help — and the most likely to turn to AI chatbots instead.

articles.title: The Obesity Drug That Was Supposed to Fix Your Liver Just Lost One in Four Patients to Side Effects
articles.excerpt: Survodutide showed impressive liver fat reduction in Phase 3 trials but a 19 per cent dropout rate from gut problems. South Asians, who carry the highest fatty liver burden globally, have reason to pay attention.
articles.image_caption: Stages of liver damage from healthy tissue to fatty liver disease and cirrhosis
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Laughter Rewires Your Child's Brain Faster Than Flashcards. The Science Says It Is Not Even Close.
articles.excerpt: New research shows laughter activates the prefrontal cortex, floods the brain with dopamine and builds resilience before children can even speak. Diaspora parents pushing academics first may want to read this twice.
articles.image_caption: Children laughing and playing together outdoors on a sunny day
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Pill Just Doubled Survival for Pancreatic Cancer. The KRAS Mutation It Targets Hits South Asians Hard.
articles.excerpt: Daraxonrasib cracked the 'undruggable' gene behind 90 per cent of pancreatic cancers. The FDA is fast-tracking it. Here is why South Asians should care.
articles.image_caption: A researcher conducts targeted therapy experiments in a cancer laboratory
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eating Processed Food Every Day Raised Dementia Risk by 58 Per Cent. Your Dadi's Kitchen Was the Opposite.
articles.excerpt: A Harvard study of 5,300 people over 10 years found that ultraprocessed foods drive cognitive decline. Traditional South Asian cooking may be the strongest defence diaspora families already have.
articles.image_caption: Packaged ultraprocessed snacks lining a supermarket aisle
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Hours of Weights a Week Cut Dementia Death Risk by 27 Per Cent. Most South Asians Are Not Lifting.
articles.excerpt: A Harvard study of 147,000 adults over 30 years found that combining resistance training with cardio slashed all-cause mortality by 45 per cent. The diaspora's favourite exercise — walking — is not enough on its own.
articles.image_caption: Resistance training — a new study links two hours of weekly weight exercise to a 27 per cent reduction in dementia death risk (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Night Owls Are Not Just Tired. They Are Lonelier, More Anxious, and Science Now Knows Why.
articles.excerpt: A new study presented at SLEEP 2026 found that 'nocturnal loneliness' — the isolation of being awake while the world sleeps — may be the hidden driver of anxiety in late sleepers. For first-gen immigrants working across time zones, the finding hits close to home.
articles.image_caption: The body's circadian rhythm — new research shows night owls face higher rates of loneliness, anxiety, and metabolic disruption (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Heat Wave Has Killed Nearly 100 People in Three Days. UP and Bihar Are in Crisis.
articles.excerpt: Hospitals in Uttar Pradesh are overwhelmed, Bihar is battling lightning deaths alongside the heat, and the monsoon is still two weeks away. For NRIs with elderly parents in the affected states, this is a welfare emergency.
articles.image_caption: Extreme heat scorches northern India — nearly 100 deaths reported in UP and Bihar
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Curcumin Supplement Industry Was Built on Retracted Research. It Is Now the Leading Cause of Herbal Liver Injury in America.
articles.excerpt: Your grandmother's haldi doodh was never the problem. But the $400 million curcumin capsule market may be — and the science behind it is falling apart.
articles.image_caption: Turmeric root and powder, a staple of South Asian cooking and traditional medicine
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The First Vaccine Designed Entirely by AI Just Passed Its Human Trial. It Needs No Needle and No Refrigerator.
articles.excerpt: Cambridge researchers used machine learning to build a 'super-antigen' that targets every known coronavirus — and the ones that haven't emerged yet. For India, the implications go beyond science.
articles.image_caption: 3D rendering of SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus particles
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two New Weight Loss Drugs Just Outperformed Wegovy With a Fraction of the Side Effects. South Asians Should Be Watching Closely.
articles.excerpt: Petrelintide cut GI side effects to near-placebo levels. Enicepatide hit 22.7 per cent weight loss in 48 weeks. The obesity drug monopoly is cracking open, and the stakes are highest for the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: Ozempic injection pen, the semaglutide-based drug now being challenged by two experimental weight loss medications (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Probiotic Pill Just Entered the Largest Cancer Trial of Its Kind. Your Dadi's Dahi May Have Been Training Your Immune System All Along.
articles.excerpt: Nearly 700 kidney cancer patients will test whether a Japanese gut bacterium can amplify immunotherapy. The science traces back to chicken farmers, but the implications land squarely on the South Asian dinner table.
articles.image_caption: Gut microbiome illustration — the trillions of bacteria now linked to cancer treatment outcomes in landmark clinical trials (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Sleeping Pill Your Doctor Prescribed May Be Wrecking Your Morning Drive. A World-First Trial Just Proved It.
articles.excerpt: Low-dose quetiapine — increasingly prescribed off-label for insomnia — impaired next-day driving and slowed reaction times. One in four people did not even notice.
articles.image_caption: Seroquel (quetiapine) 25mg tablets, increasingly prescribed off-label for insomnia despite new safety concerns
